subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value:
A HAND-WRITTEN C COPY OF AN INLINED `operator delete` BODY REPRODUCES THE ARITHMETIC BUT NOT THE `__unexpected` ISLAND, AND THE MISSING-INSTRUCTION COUNT IS THE SIGNATURE THAT FINDS THE WHOLE CLASS AT ONCE. THE SEARCH KEY, which costs one grep: any function whose `fndiff --ops` shows one or more target-only 4-instruction runs spelled exactly ['b','addi','bl','b'] (a `b` over an `addi rN,r31,K / bl __unexpected / b .` island), together with a target-only `stmw`/`lmw` pair and a `replace ['addi','addi'] <- ['mr']` at the prologue (the r31 frame-pointer alias). Each such run is ONE inlined allocator call the source is faking. Count them and grep the TU for the release idiom written out longhand; in this TU one grep for `gMovieAllocCount--` mapped 1:1 onto the four lowest-scoring functions, and the arithmetic checks before any build: fn_800D9C5C was 6 instructions short = 1 island (4) + stmw/lmw (2), fn_800D9CF4 was 10 short = 2 islands (8) + 2, fn_800DBA80 was 14 short = 3 islands (12) + 2.

THE CONVERSION. Wrap the function in its own surgical `#pragma cplusplus on/off` pair and spell it `extern "C"` so the placeholder symbol stays unmangled, then replace each hand-written `if (p) { count--; if (!count) Reset(); }` block with a call to a real inlined release whose empty exception specification supplies the island.

THREE CONSTRAINTS, each measured, and each one is where a naive attempt fails.
(1) WHICH CALLEE. `::operator delete` only inlines at call sites BELOW its definition (the case-(B) degradation of claim.law.class-scope-inline-operator-delete: at earlier sites it silently becomes `bl __dl__FPv`, the body vanishes, and the score REGRESSES). The class-scope inline operator that law prescribes is unavailable to a free function. The working form is a file-local `static inline` helper carrying `throw()`, defined once near the top of the TU. It must be a SECOND helper: this TU already had a no-throw `MovieReleaseAlloc`, and adding `throw()` to that one would have put a spurious second island in fn_800D8784, whose own `throw()` already supplies its single island (the standing law). So the rule is: caller WITHOUT its own throw() takes the throw() helper; caller WITH throw() takes the plain one.
(2) WHERE `dont_inline` GOES. `#pragma dont_inline on` suppresses the inliner for the WHOLE region, including inlining INTO the marked function -- so a dont_inline placed on the callee to keep it out of line also destroys the island conversion inside it (measured directly: the release came out as `bl MovieReleaseAllocEH`). When a function must stay out of line for its caller AND must itself inline a helper, move the pragma to the CALLER. Verified twice and gate-confirmed: fn_800D9C5C's pragma moved to MovieDecoderInitBuffers, fn_800D9CF4's to dtor_800DBB94; both callers kept their exact call and both callees gained their islands. Removing the callee-side pragma without adding the caller-side one is a real regression, and the gate catches it (MovieDecoderInitBuffers went EXACT -> STRUCTURAL, +10 instructions, when fn_800D9C5C inlined into it).
(3) THE OUTER GUARD IS NOT REDUNDANT. `if (p) Release(p);` and a bare `Release(p);` differ by one instruction: the target emits TWO consecutive `beq` to the SAME label off one un-reloaded cr0 -- the source's guard and the inlined body's own null check. Dropping the guard leaves the function exactly one `beq` short (measured on fn_800D96B0, real 23 -> 14 on restoring it).

RESIDUAL THIS DOES NOT CLOSE, so nobody re-spends it: after conversion the island's frame slot can still sit 8 bytes low (`addi r3,r31,24` vs target `addi r3,r31,32`) even when frame size, save set and slot map are all IDENTICAL -- see the companion record claim.law.MD_eh-state-slot-offset-is-not-source-reachable.
